documents.title: Bruising and nosebleeds
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I've been meaning to ask about this for a while. I bruise really easily, for a year and a half maybe, and I get nosebleeds a lot more than I used to. This week my gums are bleeding every time I brush. I also have little red dots on my shins. Is this something I should come in for? I'm free after 3 most days.

documents.title: Re: Bruising and nosebleeds
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, I'd like to see you tomorrow, and we'll check a blood count while you're here. The front desk will text you a 3:30 time. If you get a nosebleed that won't stop with 15 minutes of pressure, or any blood in urine or stool, go to the ER tonight. Skip ibuprofen and aspirin for now.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

results.test: Platelets Large [Presence] in Blood by Light microscopy
results.text: Present. Platelets decreased in number, many large forms. Red cells and white cells normal in appearance; no schistocytes, no blasts.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for bruising. Says she's bruised easily for about 18 months, figured it was bumping into desks in the classroom. Nosebleeds have gotten more frequent over the same stretch, a few a month this winter, usually stop with pressure. Since the weekend her gums bleed with brushing. Noticed tiny red spots on both shins a few days ago. No blood in urine or stool, periods not heavier than usual, no recent dental work, no new medicines or supplements, no NSAIDs, no fevers, sweats or weight loss. No bleeding with her T&A or wisdom teeth. No family history of bleeding problems.

O: Vitals as charted. Well, no distress. Scattered petechiae over both lower legs. Ecchymoses on both arms and both thighs, some yellow-green, some purple. Gums with a little dried blood at the margins, nothing active. No lymph nodes in neck, axillae or groin. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly, spleen not palpable. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P: Mucocutaneous bleeding with petechiae in an otherwise well woman. Most worried about a low platelet count. CBC with diff and smear review drawn here, asked the lab to call with the result tonight.
- No aspirin/NSAIDs, soft toothbrush, avoid contact sports and ladders.
- Bleeding precautions reviewed; ED for a nosebleed that won't stop, blood in urine or stool, severe headache.
- Will call her tonight with the count and arrange hematology.

documents.title: CBC result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lab called: platelets 11K, large platelets on smear, otherwise the count and smear look normal. Called pt at home. No active bleeding right now, gums stopped, no headache. Explained this looks like an immune process affecting platelets alone but needs hematology to confirm. Spoke with the on-call hematologist, who will see her this coming Wednesday and is comfortable with outpatient workup since she's stable with only skin and gum bleeding. Referral sent. Reviewed again: ED for any significant bleeding or headache. She will let her principal know she may need a day off.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (600 mg calcium) by mouth three times daily
Take 1 capsule (2000 IU) by mouth daily

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY GROUP
Consultation, seen 03/24/2021
Referred by: primary care, for thrombocytopenia

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Martel, a 41-year-old teacher. She describes roughly a year and a half of bruising with little or no trauma and nosebleeds that have become frequent, and in the past week bleeding from the gums with brushing. Your CBC last week showed a platelet count of 11,000 with large platelets and an otherwise unremarkable smear.

PMH: none prior. PSH: tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy age 12, third molars removed age 20. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother hypothyroid, father hypertensive, no bleeding disorders. SH: never smoker, rare alcohol, elementary teacher.

Exam: petechiae scattered over both lower extremities; several ecchymoses of differing ages on the arms and legs. No hepatosplenomegaly. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs today: Hgb 13.2 g/dL, WBC 7.2 K/uL, platelets 28 K/uL. PT 12 sec (control 11-13.5), aPTT 30 sec (control 25-35).

Impression: isolated thrombocytopenia with normal coagulation studies, normal other cell lines and large platelets on smear, without splenomegaly: immune thrombocytopenic purpura.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 10 mg daily, started today.
2. Calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily and vitamin D3 2000 IU daily while on steroid.
3. Bleeding precautions, avoid NSAIDs and aspirin.
4. Return next week with repeat counts.

Allergies: NKDA. Thank you for the referral.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY GROUP
Follow-up, seen 04/01/2021

42-year-old woman with ITP diagnosed here about a week ago. Since then more bruising, new nosebleeds and gums bleeding more with brushing. Taking prednisone 10 mg daily every morning, no side effects so far. No blood in urine, no dark stools, no headache or change in vision or strength, no falls or injuries.

Vitals stable.
Exam: new petechiae across both lower legs; ecchymoses on the forearms and thighs. Dried blood along the gumline, no active oozing. Liver and spleen not enlarged. No lymphadenopathy.

Labs: Hgb 12.3, WBC 6.9, platelets 9 K/uL. PT and aPTT normal.

Assessment: ITP, count lower this week on prednisone 10 mg.
Plan: continue prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium and vitamin D. Counts weekly through the lab near her school. Strict bleeding precautions. Call us or go to the ED for heavy bleeding, headache or blood in urine or stool.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg TID; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Checking in after her first two hematology visits. Diagnosed with ITP, started prednisone 10 mg, calcium and vitamin D. Count was 9K last week. She is going for weekly counts. Gums stopped bleeding a few days ago, one short nosebleed. Bruises fading. Sleeping a bit worse on prednisone but otherwise fine. A little anxious about it all, and about being around 8-year-olds all day, but coping; not interested in counseling right now.

Exam: vitals as charted. Fading ecchymoses on both forearms, a few petechiae at ankles. Gums clean.

A/P: ITP, under hematology. Reviewed the diagnosis together, answered questions. Reinforced precautions and no NSAIDs; acetaminophen fine for headaches. Take prednisone in the morning to help sleep. Updated her med list from the hematology letters. Note for school about limiting playground duty while her count is low. Follow up as needed; I'll keep getting the hematology letters.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
42 y/o here for her physical, first in-person one since 2019.

Interval: ITP diagnosed in March by hematology, on prednisone 10 mg daily since, with calcium carbonate 600 mg TID and D3 2000 IU. Counts have run in the 30s with a dip to 18 in early October with more bruising and nosebleeds; better since. Up about 3 kg since spring, feels hungrier on prednisone. Sleep okay if she takes it early.

ROS: no vision change, no thirst or frequent urination, no bone pain, mood fine. Bruising occasional.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP fine. A few small ecchymoses on shins, no petechiae. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft, spleen not palpable. No edema. Breast exam normal.

A/P
1. ITP, followed by hematology on prednisone 10 mg. CBC today for the shared record.
2. Long-term prednisone: A1c, vitamin D level, CMP today. Baseline DXA ordered since she has been on a steroid 8 months and counting.
3. Health maintenance: mammogram done September, normal. Pap 2023. Flu shot done 10/28. COVID booster when eligible, likely next month at the pharmacy. Lipids today.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from yesterday: platelets in the mid 30s, about where hematology has been seeing them. Sugar test (A1c) 5.3, normal. Vitamin D 36, good. Kidney, liver and cholesterol all fine. The breast center will call to schedule your bone density scan.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: glucocorticoid therapy since 03/2021. Technique: dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. No prior for comparison. Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -0.4. Left femoral neck T-score -0.8. Left total hip T-score -0.3. No vertebrae excluded.
reports.conclusion: Bone mineral density within normal limits.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrived 03/27/2022 13:20, Sunday

CC: bruising and bleeding gums x5 days, nosebleed this morning lasting ~30 min.

HPI: 42 yo F with chronic ITP since March 2021, followed by outside hematology, on prednisone 10 mg daily. Purple patches appeared on her thighs and upper arms on their own over the past 5 days. Last two days her gums bleed after brushing, and today a nosebleed went almost half an hour before it stopped. She had a mild cold about two weeks ago that cleared on its own. Denies blood in urine, black stools, heavy periods. No dental procedures or injuries. Takes no blood thinners or anti-inflammatories. No personal or family history of a bleeding disorder before the ITP.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg TID, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, social alcohol, teacher.

Vitals: within normal limits, see flowsheet.
Exam: well appearing, NAD. Ecchymoses on arms and thighs, petechiae on both lower legs. Gums mildly erythematous with dried blood, no active bleeding. Nares without active bleeding. No hepatosplenomegaly, no lymphadenopathy. Heart and lungs normal. Neuro nonfocal. Pelvic exam unremarkable.

Labs: Hgb 12.9, WBC 6.7, Plt 14.

MDM: known ITP with mucocutaneous bleeding, no active hemorrhage now, stable hemoglobin, no neurologic signs. Discussed by phone with her hematology group's on-call physician: continue current prednisone, clinic will see her this week.
Dispo: discharged home. Bleeding precautions, return for any heavy bleeding, headache, or blood in urine/stool. Follow up with hematology and PCP.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - INTERNAL MEDICINE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/03/2022, discharged 10/05/2022
PCP: copy to primary care

Admitting diagnosis: chronic immune thrombocytopenic purpura with mucocutaneous bleeding.

History: 43-year-old woman with chronic ITP since 03/2021 on prednisone 10 mg daily, seen in our ED six months ago with a similar flare. For 5 days she has had bruising and gum bleeding, with purplish patches on the thighs and upper arms that came up without injury; over the last 2 days bleeding after brushing and a nosebleed of close to 30 minutes. A mild upper respiratory infection about two weeks before admission resolved untreated. No hematuria, melena or menorrhagia. No recent dental work or trauma. Not taking anticoagulants or NSAIDs. No family history of bleeding disorders.

Exam on admission: vitals normal. Well appearing. Ecchymoses over the arms and thighs, petechiae on both lower extremities. Gums mildly erythematous with residual dried blood, no active bleeding. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy. Cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams normal. Pelvic exam unremarkable.

Labs: admission Hgb 12.9, WBC 6.7, platelets 14 K. Day of discharge platelets 68 K.

Hospital course: admitted given recurrent bleeding with a count below 20 K. Hematology consulted. IVIG 1 g/kg (70 g) given once on 10/03, tolerated without infusion reaction. No further bleeding. Count 68 K on 10/05, discharged.

Discharge medications: prednisone 10 mg daily (unchanged); calcium carbonate 600 mg TID; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: outside hematology in 2 weeks; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call within 2 business days of discharge. Home, feels fine, no bleeding since Monday. Has her discharge meds (no changes). Hospital follow-up booked 10/11, hematology 10/20.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Admitted 10/3-10/5 for another ITP flare, count 14K, same story as March (cold, then bruising, gum bleeding, long nosebleed). Got one dose of IVIG, count 68K at discharge. Home on her usual prednisone 10 mg. Feels well, no headaches after the infusion, no bleeding since. Back at school yesterday.

Exam: vitals as charted. Fading bruises on thighs and upper arms, no new petechiae. Gums fine. IV site in L antecubital healing.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP, second bleed needing hospital-level care this year. Hematology visit 10/20. Discharge summary reviewed, med list reconciled, no changes.
2. Flu vaccine today while her count is up; firm pressure, small needle.
3. Bivalent COVID booster at the pharmacy, she plans next week.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43 y/o, yearly. Rough year with the ITP: ED in March and an admission in October, both after colds, both 14K. One IVIG dose in October. Since then no bleeding. Still prednisone 10 mg daily from hematology, calcium and D. Weight steady since last fall. Working full time.

ROS otherwise negative. Mood good, PHQ-9 low.

Exam: vitals as charted. Skin with two small shin bruises, no petechiae. HEENT normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly. No edema. Breast exam normal.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg, hematology following. CBC today.
2. Steroid monitoring: A1c, CMP. DXA last December normal.
3. Health maintenance: mammogram September normal. Flu 10/11, bivalent COVID 10/20. Pap next year.
RTC 6 months for a steroid check-in, physical next fall.
